title: Kale, frozen, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt

content.title: About
content.content: Kale (Brassica oleracea var. acephala) is a leafy cruciferous vegetable. Frozen, boiled and drained without added salt, it retains most of its nutrients, a mildly bitter flavor and a firm texture after cooking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Kale is often called a “superfood” because of its high vitamin and antioxidant content.
Ancient Romans used kale as a medicinal herb.
Kale can thrive in cold climates, making it a common crop in northern regions.
Leaves may be curly or flat (the “Lacinato” or dinosaur kale variety).
Blanching before freezing helps preserve chlorophyll and carotenoids.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Kale provides over 700% of the daily value for vitamin K, essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: High in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Abundant antioxidants
items.content: Kale contains carotenoids, quercetin and kaempferol, which protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Source of calcium and magnesium
items.content: These minerals are important for bones, muscles and nerve function.

items.title: Low‑calorie plant protein
items.content: One cup of boiled kale delivers about 3 g of protein with very few calories.

items.title: Thyroid considerations
items.content: Kale contains glucosinolates that may affect thyroid function when consumed in very large amounts.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large quantities of raw kale can cause gas; cooking reduces this effect.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: A small number of people may be allergic to cruciferous vegetables.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Boiled, unsalted kale can be added to soups, stews, salads, smoothies, or served as a side dish. It also mixes well with grains, legumes and meat dishes to boost nutritional value.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen boiled kale in an airtight container at –18 °C. Once thawed, use within 2–3 days and do not refreeze.
